title: 2021 AMC 12B Problem 19
statement: Two fair dice, each with at least \(6\) faces are rolled. On each face of each die is printed a distinct integer from \(1\) to the number of faces on that die, inclusive. The probability of rolling a sum of \(7\) is \(\dfrac34\) of the probability of rolling a sum of \(10,\) and the probability of rolling a sum of \(12\) is \(\dfrac{1}{12}.\) What is the least possible number of faces on the two dice combined?

solutions.text:
Let the dice have \(a\le b\) faces. Since both have at least \(6\) faces, a sum of \(7\) occurs in exactly \(6\) ways, so a sum of \(10\) occurs in \(6\div\tfrac34=8\) ways.

The number of ways to roll \(10\) is \(\min(a,9)\) \(-\max(1,10-b)+1=8.\) A sum of \(12\) has probability \(\tfrac{1}{12},\) so it occurs in \(\tfrac{ab}{12}\) ways.

Having \(8\) outcomes for a sum of \(10\) requires \(a\ge8\) and \(b\ge9,\) so necessarily \(a+b\ge17.\) For \((a,b)=(8,9),\) a sum of \(10\) has \(8\) outcomes, while a sum of \(12\) has the \(6\) outcomes with the first die showing \(3,4,\ldots,8.\) Since \(\frac{6}{8\cdot9}=\frac{1}{12},\) both conditions hold and the lower bound \(17\) is attained.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: With at least \(6\) faces each, a sum of \(7\) always has \(6\) ways, so a sum of \(10\) has \(8\) ways
Let the dice have \(a\le b\) faces; count outcomes for sums \(10\) and \(12\) and use \(\text{ways}(12)=\tfrac{ab}{12}\)
